newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Northam braced for NUM strike over wages.
newsitem.headline: Northam braced for NUM strike over wages.

text.p: South Africa's Northam Platinum Ltd said on Monday it was braced for a strike by members of the National Union of Mineworkrs (NUM) who were being balloted on Monday and Tuesday over wages.
"We have in fact reached deadlock with the union. Strike ballots are taking place as we are speaking," chairman Peter Janisch told reporters at a quarterly results presentation.
"We hope it will not necessarily lead to a strike but we have to be prepared for it."
The mine, which produced 75,365 ounces of precious metals in concentrates in the three months to September, has some 5,500 workers of whom 3,300 belong to the NUM.
The remaining employees have already accepted a 10 percent increase under the annual wage review but deadlock was reached with the NUM on September 27.

Northam, part of Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, recorded a net loss before capital spending of 7.39 million rand in the September quarter after turning in a profit of 8.17 million in the previous quarter.
